story.lore.l01.title: A Repair Brief
story.lore.l01.body:
Apprentice,

The western bell has stopped shedding rain. Do not strike it harder. Clear the dust from its lip, then watch which way the hanging thread moves. The bell measures the difference between the intake and the release; it does not make water.

Begin at Bamboo Hollow. Inspect the reader before you reconnect anything. If the needle crosses the red notch, leave the return channel open and come home.

I have taken the others downriver. The villages need a warning delivered by a person, not another sealed notice. Lan knows the paths. Listen when he speaks about water.

— Yun
story.lore.l02.title: Supply Porter Register
story.lore.l02.body:
New hand: the porter from the south stair. No recommendation seal. Knows how to lash a crate and checks a bridge before stepping on it.

Asked whether a person without a family manual could learn here. I said yes. Asked what the fees were. I said a week of clearing the gutters would do, and they looked offended on behalf of the gutters.

Give them the plain practice sword. The fine one is too heavy. Cultivation can wait until they stop holding their breath on every swing.

I have entered their name in the apprentice column, not the porter column.

— Lan
story.lore.l03.title: Waterwheel Tally
story.lore.l03.body:
First frost: wheel turns through the evening.
Second frost: wheel stops before supper.
Third frost: moved the millstone to the hand frame. Four families now take turns; do not put the little ones on the night shift.

The mountain report calls this a reduction in downstream demand. We still need flour. The report means there is less water, not less hunger.

Whoever comes to read the marker: use the lower stair. The old path is marked safe on your map, but two steps are gone. I have tied reeds across it.

— A mill keeper
story.lore.l04.title: The Reed Knot
story.lore.l04.body:
Two knots mean the next landing is sound. Three mean there is someone waiting below. One loose reed means turn back and check the bank; it is not a direction marker.

Do not replace these with painted arrows. Paint stays on a wall after the water has moved. A knot is changed by the last person who walked the stair.

If you find a broken mark, make it plain before you leave. You do not have to be a warden to warn the next traveller.

On the back: A small child's uneven drawing of a waterwheel, repaired twice in darker ink.
story.lore.l05.title: Mei's Lunch Note
story.lore.l05.body:
Brother,

The rice is in the blue pot. The lid sticks. Do not ask the child next door to open it for you again.

I am checking the east spillway. They have changed the gate number but not the signs at the fork. Someone will follow the old number into the flood ditch. I will repaint it before the market crowd comes through.

The lamp needs a new handle. I have wrapped it for today. You promised to fix it last week.

Save me the sour plums. This is not a formal request.

— Mei
story.lore.l06.title: A Bypass With No Number
story.lore.l06.body:
I opened the narrow return after the second refusal. It brought the lower pools up by half a hand. The fields thawed three days later.

The needle at the intake has climbed since. I wrote it down and still left the return open.

This page will not make the decision right. It will make the decision visible to whoever has to mend it after me. The channel is mine. The winters that made it necessary are not.

If Yun returns before I speak to the apprentice, show him this page.

— Lan
story.lore.l06.inspect: Read A Bypass With No Number
